A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite appendix reorganization and one removed experiment.

before.justification: V1 reports original feedback annotations, detection evaluations, response-regeneration comparisons, and fine-tuning results on MTBench and WildBench, including additional Qwen results in Appendix F.

after.justification: V2 retains original annotation, detection, response-regeneration, and fine-tuning results in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The feedback classifier, semantic response regeneration, regeneration-from-scratch procedure, and SFT objective are unchanged. Removing the Qwen evaluation does not revise the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions use LMSYS and WildChat interactions, MTBench and WildBench evaluation tasks, and the LIMA prompt-quality comparison. The removed Qwen experiment changes model coverage, not datasets or task requirements.

E2.justification: The prior feedback-detection prompt, KTO, regeneration-from-scratch controls, and original-response comparisons remain unchanged. The deleted Qwen experiment applies existing comparison methods to another backbone; it introduces no distinct comparator method.

E3.justification: V2 removes the additional Qwen1.5-4B configuration described in v1 Section 7.2 and Appendix F, leaving Vicuna-7B and Mistral-7B for fine-tuning evaluation. Retained training budgets, sample sizes, metrics, and judges are unchanged. The 500-question WildBench subset description merely moves from a footnote into the main text.

E4.justification: The feedback-distribution, toxicity, refusal, prompt-quality, judge-comparison, and illustrative case analyses are retained. The deleted Qwen table reports additional backbone benchmark results rather than a separate ablation or robustness protocol.

E5.justification: Both versions report average performance and variance over five randomly initialized training runs and retain the same paired t-tests. V1 Appendix I/Table 17 becomes v2 Appendix G/Table 9 without changing the statistical reporting.

E6.justification: V1 Table 14's seven Qwen MTBench result entries are removed, including the 4.96 base score and 6.31±0.07 score after training on WildChat semantic regenerations. All matched main-text and appendix tables retain identical numerical values; the plotted findings are also unchanged.

T1.justification: The conversation and label-set definitions, feedback-selected subsets, regeneration equations, and reward-model formulations are unchanged. Neither version introduces additional theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: V2 removes the abstract's claim that feedback usefulness is largely tied to initial-prompt quality. The central contributions and the claim of mixed benefits across MTBench and WildBench remain, as does the conclusion.

C2.justification: The introduction adds older models' limited ability to integrate feedback as a reason for the distillation setting. Section 6.1 qualifies its heading from 'Adding feedback semantics doesn't help' to 'doesn't always help.' The detailed benchmark interpretations and Limitations section otherwise remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The reported A100 hardware, 5e-6 learning rate, approximately two-hour training runs, feedback-detection prompt, and code/data access statement and link are retained. Moving evaluation details and the prompt appendix does not add reproducibility information; the new computing acknowledgement supplies no additional experimental specifications.

R1.justification: V2 removes four references from the introduction's ambiguity discussion: Cole et al. (2023), Zhang and Choi (2023), and the two Zhang et al. (2024) papers. It also removes the Qwen1.5 reference with that experiment. Section 8's substantive research positioning is unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 lightly edits the abstract and introduction, corrects several typos, and adds an Empire AI computing acknowledgement. It moves Feedback Detection from Appendix C to Appendix H and renumbers the intervening appendices, while retaining the main section structure and most prose.

P2.justification: The Qwen results table is removed, and appendix figures and tables are redistributed closer to their associated sections. The benchmark-characteristics table is placed beside its explanatory text. The six figures and retained table designs are otherwise substantially unchanged.

improvement.justification: V2 improves wording and appendix organization, but removes the Qwen1.5-4B validation in v1 Appendix F/Table 14 without replacement. That experiment tested an additional, newer model family and documented dataset-dependent benefits, so its removal modestly weakens the breadth of the fine-tuning evidence. This limited evidential loss outweighs the small presentation gains; the core results and statistical support remain unchanged.
